invocation.name: Dead-link check (.md → .md)
invocation.run:
while IFS= read -r src; do
  # shellcheck disable=SC2016  # regex literal, no expansion intended
  grep -oE '`[^`]*\.md`' "$src" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '`' | sort -u | while read -r ref; do
    case "$ref" in
      # AIF convention rename targets (template → final name) — not real files in the repo
      *.ai-factory/*|*AGENTS.md|*CLAUDE.md|*DESCRIPTION.md|*ARCHITECTURE.md|*.template.md|*\<*) continue ;;
      docs/architecture.md) continue ;;  # used as anti-pattern example
    esac
    base=$(basename "$ref")
    if ! find . -name "$base" -not -path "./.git/*" 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
      echo "::warning file=$src::dead .md reference → $ref"
    fi
  done
  # historical audit reports may reference suggested filenames / anti-patterns
done < <(find . -name "*.md" -not -path "./.git/*" -not -name "audit-results-*.md" -not -path "./docs/audits/*")

name: Every R-rule has probe / manual / ESLint delegation

invocation.name: Every R-rule has probe / manual / ESLint delegation
invocation.run:
fail=0
for rules_file in packages/preset-next-15-canonical/RULES.md packages/preset-next-15-canonical/RULES.react-next.md; do
  # ^## R<digits>[<lowercase>]?  — matches R1..R20, R16a/R16b; excludes "## Rule maintenance"
  while IFS= read -r r; do
    in_audit=0
    # skip_unless R<n>[a-z]*  — covers R16 → R16a/R16b sub-probes
    # Wave 10.4: also grep *.ts (audit-ai-docs.ts replaced audit-ai-docs.sh)
    grep -qE "skip_unless ${r}[a-z]*\b" packages/core/audit-self/*.sh packages/core/audit-self/*.ts packages/preset-next-15-canonical/audit-self/*.sh 2>/dev/null && in_audit=1
    in_manual=0
    # Wave 10.4: agents/best-practices-sidecar.md removed in PR #79; markers now in *.ts.
    # Use find+xargs to avoid nonexistent-file exit-code-2 masking valid matches.
    if find packages/core/audit-self packages/preset-next-15-canonical/audit-self \( -name "*.sh" -o -name "*.ts" \) -print0 2>/dev/null | \
       xargs -0 grep -qE "$r.*manual|manual.*$r|$r.*delegated|delegated.*$r" 2>/dev/null; then
      in_manual=1
    fi
    if [ "$in_audit" -eq 0 ] && [ "$in_manual" -eq 0 ]; then
      echo "::error::orphan rule $r — no probe, no manual review note, no delegation"
      fail=1
    fi
  done < <(grep -oE "^## R[0-9]+[a-z]?" "$rules_file" | grep -oE "R[0-9]+[a-z]?")
done
exit "$fail"

name: Run getff go lane live-fire (adapter-jig J3)

invocation.name: Run getff go lane live-fire (adapter-jig J3)
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail
# Scratch fixture: a fresh Go module in an OS temp dir, then install.sh go fires the lane's
# _go_firing_self_check (F8). The self-check plants a violating .go file (os.Getenv) in its
# OWN mktemp -d, asserts golangci-lint fires RED on the violation + GREEN on the clean control,
# prints ✓-prefixed PASS lines. The self-check returns 0 on EVERY branch by contract (F8
# mandates rc=0 always so a self-check never aborts install.sh) — so the step cannot rely
# on exit code alone. We capture the output and grep for the lane's OWN failure markers.
# MAJOR 2 fix (pre-egress fidelity audit 2026-07-25): the previous version asserted only
# artefact existence, which proves DELIVERY but not FIRING — a SILENT or OVER-BROAD config
# prints its ✗ marker and the step still went GREEN. Now: the step fails on any ✗ / ⚠
# degrade line (on this runner the toolchain IS present, so a degrade means the install
# step did not take effect), and asserts the positive «enforcement is live» line is present.
fixture="$(mktemp -d)"
printf 'module example.com/j3-livefire\n\ngo 1.22\n' > "$fixture/go.mod"
cd "$fixture"
# Tee captures the install.sh output (including _go_firing_self_check markers) to a log
# AND surfaces it to the GitHub Actions step log for operator visibility.
bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/install.sh" go 2>&1 | tee /tmp/j3-go-livefire.log
# Re-affirm the lane delivered the artefacts the firing self-check attested against:
[ -f "$fixture/.golangci.yml" ] || { echo "❌ J3 live-fire: .golangci.yml not delivered"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$fixture/.github/workflows/getff-go.yml" ] || { echo "❌ J3 live-fire: getff-go.yml not delivered"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$fixture/.ai-factory/synthesizer-output/rules-lock.go.json" ] || { echo "❌ J3 live-fire: rules-lock.go.json not emitted"; exit 1; }
# FIRING assertions (the load-bearing half — artefact existence alone is delivery, not firing):
#  (a) on this runner go AND golangci-lint ARE present (installed in the previous step),
#      so a "NOT proven (tool absent)" degrade line means the install did not take effect.
#  (b) a SILENT config (golangci-lint does not fire on the planted os.Getenv violation)
#      or an OVER-BROAD one (it fires on the clean control) is a delivery bug; the self-check
#      prints ✗ for both. The summary line repeats SILENT/OVER-BROAD/NOT proven tokens.
if grep -E 'SILENT|OVER-BROAD|NOT proven \(tool absent\)|✗' /tmp/j3-go-livefire.log; then
  echo "❌ J3 live-fire: firing self-check produced a failure marker (see lines above)"
  exit 1
fi
# Assert the POSITIVE too: the lane MUST print the «enforcement is live» summary, proving
# both directions fired correctly. Its absence means the self-check did not run at all
# (a worse failure than a wrong config — the lane silently skipped its own proof).
if ! grep -F 'enforcement is live' /tmp/j3-go-livefire.log; then
  echo "❌ J3 live-fire: «enforcement is live» summary line absent — self-check did not complete successfully"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✓ J3 go lane live-fire: artefacts delivered + firing self-check proven on the pinned go 1.22.0 + golangci-lint v1.55.2 toolchain"

invocation.name: install-sh — lychee-shipped-md-offline (consumer first-push link integrity, 2026-07-10 smoke)
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail
curl -sSfL https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-v0.24.2/lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee.tgz"
echo "1f4e0ef7f6554a6ed33dd7ac144fb2e1bbed98598e7af973042fc5cd43951c9a  $RUNNER_TEMP/lychee.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee.tgz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP" --strip-components=1
"$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee" --version
PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP:$PATH" bash tests/install-sh/lychee-shipped-md-offline.test.sh | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee-test.out"
if grep -qF 'SKIP: lychee not on PATH' "$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee-test.out"; then
  echo "::error::lychee-shipped-md-offline self-skipped despite the pinned install — this CI arm is vacuous; fix the PATH/extraction above"
  exit 1
fi

name: install-sh — shellcheck gate: setup.d/*.sh + install.sh + scripts/*.sh + scripts/lib/*.sh + the two B1 carrier scripts (pinned 0.9.0)

invocation.name: install-sh — shellcheck gate: setup.d/*.sh + install.sh + scripts/*.sh + scripts/lib/*.sh + the two B1 carrier scripts (pinned 0.9.0)
invocation.run:
if command -v shellcheck >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  shellcheck --version | grep -E '^version:' || true
  # `scripts/*.sh` does NOT recurse: scripts/lib/*.sh (the claudeMdExcludes SSOT and
  # its test) would ship unscanned, which is the same class of hole this gate exists
  # to close. `-x -P SCRIPTDIR` makes shellcheck FOLLOW the `. lib/...` source lines
  # instead of emitting SC1091 for them — the lib is then checked in its callers'
  # context, not merely as a standalone file.
  shellcheck -x -P SCRIPTDIR --exclude=SC2034,SC2016,SC2317 \
    setup.d/*.sh install.sh scripts/*.sh scripts/lib/*.sh \
    packages/core/audit-self/pre-merge-local.sh \
    packages/core/audit-self/ci-available-probe.sh
else
  echo "⊝ shellcheck not available in CI runner — skipping (install shellcheck >= 0.9.0 to enable)"
fi

name: Verify .husky/ hooks exist and are executable

invocation.name: Verify .husky/ hooks exist and are executable
invocation.run:
for hook in .husky/pre-commit .husky/pre-push; do
  test -f "$hook" || { echo "::error::missing $hook"; exit 1; }
  test -x "$hook" || { echo "::error::$hook not executable"; exit 1; }
  # non-empty + non-trivial (not just exit 0). Wave 10.1: the pre-push
  # hook may delegate its probes to the TS orchestrator
  # (packages/core/hooks/pre-push.ts) rather than inline them, so the
  # dispatch reference counts as non-trivial too.
  grep -qE '\b(actionlint|zizmor|bash -n|json\.load|yaml\.safe_load)\b|packages/core/hooks/pre-push\.ts' "$hook" \
    || { echo "::error::$hook lacks expected probes (looks empty/stub)"; exit 1; }
done
echo "✓ .husky/ hooks present, executable, non-trivial"

name: Fresh install.sh ts-server --full into a multi-stack monorepo consumer

invocation.name: Fresh install.sh ts-server --full into a multi-stack monorepo consumer
invocation.run:
CONSUMER=$(mktemp -d)
cd "$CONSUMER"
git init --quiet
git config user.email "ci@example.com"
git config user.name "CI"
# npm-managed multi-stack monorepo: apps/api (ts-server) + apps/mobile (Expo). NO
# pnpm-workspace.yaml — per-workspace detection (_workspace_pkg_dirs) keys on the
# apps/*/package.json dir-walk, NOT a pnpm manifest, so the multi-stack branch still fires;
# meanwhile detect_pm falls to npm (the runner has npm, not pnpm) so `--full` actually
# installs the toolchain. No workspace marker + no root src → AIF_ARCH_TARGET resolves to "."
# (setup.d/lib.sh:3471-3479, merge_canonical_scripts) — the same safe target the green flat job uses.
# Root carries NO deps (exactly like the flat job): install.sh adds its 22 DEVDEPS and npm
# auto-installs the typescript-eslint peer typescript. A root `typescript` pin here caused an
# ERESOLVE/ETARGET on the first run (a non-existent 5.6.0 exact). Per-workspace `typescript`
# keys below are detection SIGNALS only (never npm-resolved — no "workspaces" field).
echo '{"name":"timeliner-mono","version":"0.0.0","private":true}' > package.json
# apps/api → ts-server (Hono). A boundary source file under src/routes so check:globs
# exercises the real glob-liveness recursion (not the trivial "no source → skip").
mkdir -p apps/api/src/routes
echo '{"name":"@timeliner/api","dependencies":{"hono":"4.0.0"},"devDependencies":{"typescript":"5.6.0"}}' > apps/api/package.json
printf 'export const users = 1;\n' > apps/api/src/routes/users.ts
# apps/mobile → react-native/Expo (ships NO RULE_GLOBS.boundary → the gate skips it).
mkdir -p apps/mobile
echo '{"name":"@timeliner/mobile","dependencies":{"expo":"~52.0.0","react-native":"0.76.0","react":"18.3.0"}}' > apps/mobile/package.json
# XFAIL (known install gap, surfaced by critical-review wave 2): with no "workspaces" field
# nothing installs apps/mobile's own deps, so the placed apps/mobile/eslint.config.mjs cannot
# load eslint-config-expo and self-verify fences-fire FAILs. The install used to print
# «✅ Installation complete» over that FAIL; it now exits 1 (S4-8). Tolerate exactly that one
# failure and nothing else — any other ✗ line, or any other rc, is RED. When the gap is fixed
# the install exits 0 and this step goes RED on purpose: drop the tolerance then.
set +e
bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/install.sh" ts-server --full > "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log" 2>&1
INSTALL_RC=$?
set -e
cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log"
if [ "$INSTALL_RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::install exited 0 — the known apps/mobile eslint-config-expo self-verify FAIL no longer reproduces; drop the XFAIL tolerance in this step"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$INSTALL_RC" -eq 1 ] || { echo "::error::install exited $INSTALL_RC (only 1 = self-verify FAILED is tolerated)"; exit 1; }
grep -q "Installation finished, but self-verify FAILED" "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log" \
  || { echo "::error::install exited 1 without the self-verify FAILED banner — a real install failure"; exit 1; }
grep -q "✗ load-probe: placed apps/mobile/eslint.config.mjs NON-LOADABLE (Cannot find package 'eslint-config-expo'" "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log" \
  || { echo "::error::self-verify FAILED, but not on the known apps/mobile eslint-config-expo gap"; exit 1; }
UNEXPECTED=$(grep '✗' "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log" \
  | grep -v "✗ load-probe: placed apps/mobile/eslint.config.mjs NON-LOADABLE (Cannot find package 'eslint-config-expo'" \
  | grep -v '✗ fences-fire FAILED' || true)
[ -z "$UNEXPECTED" ] || { echo "::error::unexpected self-verify failure(s): $UNEXPECTED"; exit 1; }
echo "✓ install ran to the end; the only self-verify FAIL is the known apps/mobile eslint-config-expo gap (XFAIL)"
echo "CONSUMER=$CONSUMER" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

name: Emit a declarative forbid bundle, verify clean, then prove it reds on a hand-edit

invocation.name: Emit a declarative forbid bundle, verify clean, then prove it reds on a hand-edit
invocation.run:
# S5: the synthesizer is the SOLE writer of emitted rule files. This job
# proves both directions in CI — a clean generator output verifies (exit 0),
# and a hand-edit of the emitted rule content reds the verifier (exit 1).
FIXTURE="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/packages/core/synthesizer/fixtures/s4-declarative-research-plan.json"
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
npm --prefix packages/core run synth --silent -- --from-research "$FIXTURE" --output "$TMP" > /dev/null

# [1] clean bundle must pass.
set +e
npm --prefix packages/core run verify:provenance --silent -- "$TMP"
CLEAN_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$CLEAN_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::S5 gate red on a freshly-emitted (un-edited) bundle — false positive (rc=$CLEAN_RC)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✓ clean emitted bundle verifies (exit 0)"

# [2] hand-edit one rule field in the emitted manifest (provenance left stale).
M="$TMP/rules-manifest-additions.json"
FIRST=$(jq -r 'keys[0]' "$M")
jq --arg id "$FIRST" '.[$id].examples.bad += "\n// hand-edited"' "$M" > "$M.tmp"
mv "$M.tmp" "$M"

# [3] verifier MUST red on the hand-edit (the прогнанный отказ, not "should bе").
set +e
npm --prefix packages/core run verify:provenance --silent -- "$TMP"
EDITED_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$EDITED_RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::S5 anti-hand-edit gate FAILED to detect a hand-edit (verify exited 0 on a corrupted bundle)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "✓ S5 anti-hand-edit gate reds on a hand-edited generated file (exit $EDITED_RC)"

invocation.name: Run zizmor
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail
# Newline-delimited string + xargs, NOT `mapfile`/arrays: the same block
# has to stay reproducible by hand on a maintainer Mac, whose /bin/bash is
# 3.2 (no mapfile; `${#arr[@]}` on an empty array trips `set -u`). Tracked
# workflow paths carry no whitespace, so word-splitting via xargs is safe.
# `|| true` keeps the empty case reaching the explicit error below instead
# of dying on grep's exit 1 under `set -e`.
TEMPLATES="$(git ls-files '*github-actions*.yml' | grep -v '^\.github/' | sort || true)"
if [ -z "$TEMPLATES" ]; then
  echo "::error::zizmor template discovery matched NOTHING — the shipped-template scan would be a silent no-op"
  exit 1
fi
printf 'Scanning %s shipped CI template(s):\n' "$(printf '%s\n' "$TEMPLATES" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
printf '%s\n' "$TEMPLATES" | sed 's/^/  /'
printf '%s\n' "$TEMPLATES" | xargs zizmor --format plain .github/workflows/

name: Resolve the gate range for this event

invocation.name: Resolve the gate range for this event
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail
BASE_REF="${BASE_REF#refs/heads/}"
case "$EVENT" in
  pull_request)
    # The checkout is the merge ref; its FIRST parent is the exact base tree it was
    # built on. Re-fetching origin/<base> instead would compare a moved base against
    # a stale merge (a re-run reuses github.sha), and a page edited on the base in
    # between would read as `refreshed`. Refuse, never skip, if HEAD is not a merge.
    git rev-parse --verify --quiet "HEAD^2" >/dev/null \
      || { echo "::error::pull_request checkout is not a merge commit — refusing to guess the D26 range"; exit 1; }
    echo "GATE_RANGE=HEAD^1..HEAD" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ;;
  merge_group)
    git fetch --no-tags --quiet origin "${BASE_REF}:refs/remotes/origin/${BASE_REF}"
    git rev-parse --verify "origin/${BASE_REF}" >/dev/null \
      || { echo "::error::base ref origin/${BASE_REF} not resolvable — refusing to run with an empty range (the D26 gate would falsely pass)"; exit 1; }
    echo "GATE_RANGE=origin/${BASE_REF}..HEAD" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ;;
  push)
    # A new branch pushes with an all-zero `before`: no ancestor range
    # exists. Skipping is safe here (not a #warning-nobody-reads hole):
    # the same commits are gated at the merge by the pull_request arm,
    # whose base ref always resolves, and on host seats by the pre-push
    # section. A non-zero `before` is the post-merge trunk check.
    if [ "$BEFORE" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
      echo "::warning::push created a branch (all-zero 'before') — no range to gate; the pull_request arm covers these commits at merge time"
      echo "GATE_RANGE=" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    else
      echo "GATE_RANGE=${BEFORE}..${AFTER}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    fi
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::unhandled event '$EVENT' for the docs-refresh gate"; exit 1 ;;
esac

invocation.name: Trigger Context7 refresh
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail

# Fail LOUDLY, never warn-and-pass: a refresh that silently no-ops is
# `#warning-nobody-reads` (.claude/rules/attention-is-not-a-mechanism.md §2). This is
# safe to fail hard because the job reports on no pull request (see the marker above),
# so a red run here cannot block any merge — it only reddens `staging`'s own history
# until the maintainer legs below are done.
#
# ONE documented carve-out, matched on the exact response: the service enforces a
# 10-day minimum between refreshes and answers HTTP 400 with
# {"error":"too-early", ...} for the nine days after any successful refresh. That
# body means the index is already fresh — a no-op, not a defect — so exactly that
# error token in the body is treated as success. Everything else still exits
# non-zero: an unset key (below), a 401, any other 4xx/5xx body, a network failure.
# No `|| true`, no dropped `--fail-with-body`, no `continue-on-error` — those would
# convert this gate into the `#warning-nobody-reads` pattern this job refuses.
if [ -z "${CONTEXT7_API_KEY}" ]; then
  echo "::error::CONTEXT7_API_KEY is unset. Two maintainer actions are required, in order: (1) submit ${LIBRARY_NAME} at https://context7.com/add-library so the library exists; (2) add the CONTEXT7_API_KEY repository secret from https://context7.com/dashboard. Until both are done this workflow cannot succeed."
  exit 1
fi

refresh_rc=0
body="$(curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST https://context7.com/api/v1/refresh \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CONTEXT7_API_KEY}" \
  -d "{\"libraryName\": \"${LIBRARY_NAME}\"}")" || refresh_rc=$?

echo "${body}"
echo
if [ "${refresh_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "Refresh requested for ${LIBRARY_NAME}."
  exit 0
fi

# curl exit 22 = --fail-with-body tripped on an HTTP error status; the body it
# printed is echoed above. Only the documented too-early body is the no-op success.
if [ "${refresh_rc}" -eq 22 ] && printf '%s' "${body}" | grep -q '"error":"too-early"'; then
  echo "Context7 index for ${LIBRARY_NAME} is already fresh: service answered too-early (10-day minimum between refreshes). Nothing to do — treated as success."
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::Context7 refresh failed for ${LIBRARY_NAME} (curl exit ${refresh_rc}; body above)."
exit "${refresh_rc}"

name: Check PR body for §1.7 sections or skip marker

invocation.name: Check PR body for §1.7 sections or skip marker
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail

if [ -z "${PR_BODY:-}" ]; then
  echo "::error::PR description is empty. PR touches discipline-bearing files."
  echo "Required: ### §1.7 Forward-check applied + ### §1.7 Backward-check applied"
  echo "Or: ### §1.7 Skipped: <rationale ≥60 chars>"
  echo "See: .claude/rules/phase-research-coverage.md §1.7"
  exit 1
fi

# Skip marker shortcuts the gate. Body must be ≥60 chars after the colon.
if echo "$PR_BODY" | grep -qE '^### §1\.7 Skipped:.{60,}'; then
  echo "✅ §1.7 Skipped marker present with ≥60-char rationale."
  exit 0
fi

# Extract section bodies via awk: from "### §1.7 <Section>" to next "###"
forward_body=$(echo "$PR_BODY" | awk '
  /^### §1\.7 Forward-check applied/ { capture=1; next }
  /^###/ { capture=0 }
  capture { print }
' | tr -d '[:space:]' | wc -c)

backward_body=$(echo "$PR_BODY" | awk '
  /^### §1\.7 Backward-check applied/ { capture=1; next }
  /^###/ { capture=0 }
  capture { print }
' | tr -d '[:space:]' | wc -c)

fail=0
if [ "$forward_body" -lt 40 ]; then
  echo "::error::Missing or too-short \"### §1.7 Forward-check applied\" section (${forward_body} non-whitespace chars, need ≥40)."
  fail=1
fi
if [ "$backward_body" -lt 40 ]; then
  echo "::error::Missing or too-short \"### §1.7 Backward-check applied\" section (${backward_body} non-whitespace chars, need ≥40)."
  fail=1
fi

if [ "$fail" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "PR touches discipline-bearing files (.claude/rules/, packages/core/principles/, EXECUTION-PLAN, prior-art-evaluations, CLAUDE.md, or shipped templates)."
  echo ""
  echo "PR description must include either:"
  echo "  ### §1.7 Forward-check applied"
  echo "  <body ≥40 chars enumerating which existing disciplines were checked>"
  echo ""
  echo "  ### §1.7 Backward-check applied"
  echo "  <body ≥40 chars enumerating the sweep of existing artefacts under the new rule's scope>"
  echo ""
  echo "OR a skip marker:"
  echo "  ### §1.7 Skipped: <reason ≥60 chars>"
  echo ""
  echo "Reference: .claude/rules/phase-research-coverage.md §1.7"
  echo "Skill:     .claude/skills/self-reflection/SKILL.md"
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ §1.7 sections present and non-empty (forward: ${forward_body} chars, backward: ${backward_body} chars)."

# Substance gate: Forward-check section must cite at least one file:line ref.
# Catches generic prose like "Checked existing rules R1-R20 — compliant."
# Regex: at-least-one non-whitespace path component ending in .ext:N
forward_citations=$(echo "$PR_BODY" | awk '
  /^### §1\.7 Forward-check applied/ { capture=1; next }
  /^###/ { capture=0 }
  capture { print }
' | grep -cE '[^[:space:]]+\.[a-z]+:[0-9]+' || true)

if [ "$forward_citations" -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "::error::Forward-check section contains 0 file:line citations (regex [^[:space:]]+\\.[a-z]+:[0-9]+)."
  echo "Substance arm (Wave 8.1) — §1.7 must cite specific evidence, not generic prose."
  echo "Example: 'packages/core/principles/02-paired-negative-test.test.ts:82 mutation arm verified'" # cite:historical example text for the trailer shape, not a live pointer
  echo "Bootstrap exemption: §1.7 Skipped marker with rationale ≥60 chars."
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ Forward-check cites ${forward_citations} file:line reference(s)."

# Substance gate: Backward-check section must cite at least one file:line ref
# (parity with Forward-check Wave 8.1 substance arm). Catches quantifier
# confabulation: prose like "all 13 X audited" without any verifiable citation.
# Regex: at-least-one non-whitespace path component ending in .ext:N
backward_citations=$(echo "$PR_BODY" | awk '
  /^### §1\.7 Backward-check applied/ { capture=1; next }
  /^###/ { capture=0 }
  capture { print }
' | grep -cE '[^[:space:]]+\.[a-z]+:[0-9]+' || true)

if [ "$backward_citations" -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "::error::Backward-check section contains 0 file:line citations (regex [^[:space:]]+\\.[a-z]+:[0-9]+)."
  echo "Substance arm (Forward-check Wave 8.1 parity) — §1.7 Backward-check must cite specific evidence, not generic prose."
  echo "Example: 'packages/core/hooks/checks/s17.test.ts:16 all body-prose test cases ported to vitest (Wave 10.3)'"
  echo "Bootstrap exemption: §1.7 Skipped marker with rationale ≥60 chars."
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ Backward-check cites ${backward_citations} file:line reference(s)."

name: Append snapshot row to data/metrics.csv on the data/metrics branch

invocation.name: Append snapshot row to data/metrics.csv on the data/metrics branch
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail
git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

HEADER="date,stars,forks,clones_count_14d,clones_uniques_14d,views_count_14d,views_uniques_14d"
TODAY="$(date -u +%F)"
ROW="${TODAY},${STARS},${FORKS},${CLONES_COUNT:-},${CLONES_UNIQUES:-},${VIEWS_COUNT:-},${VIEWS_UNIQUES:-}"

if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin data/metrics >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  git fetch origin data/metrics --depth=1
  git checkout -B data/metrics origin/data/metrics
else
  git checkout --orphan data/metrics
  git rm -rf . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  mkdir -p data
  echo "$HEADER" > data/metrics.csv
  git add data/metrics.csv
  git commit -q -m "chore(metrics): initialize data/metrics branch"
fi

mkdir -p data
[ -f data/metrics.csv ] || echo "$HEADER" > data/metrics.csv

# Idempotent re-runs (e.g. manual workflow_dispatch same day): drop
# any existing row for today before appending the fresh one instead
# of duplicating it.
grep -v "^${TODAY}," data/metrics.csv > data/metrics.csv.tmp || true
mv data/metrics.csv.tmp data/metrics.csv
echo "$ROW" >> data/metrics.csv

git add data/metrics.csv
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "No metrics change to commit."
else
  git commit -q -m "chore(metrics): snapshot ${TODAY}"
  git push origin data/metrics
fi

name: Compare the live manifest against origin/main

invocation.name: Compare the live manifest against origin/main
invocation.run:
set -euo pipefail
main_sha="$(git rev-parse origin/main)"
echo "pin-freshness: framework origin/main = ${main_sha}"

# Fail-closed fetch: a 404 (the landing does not serve the manifest yet) or any
# transport error is a RED, never a skip. (rc captured before the branch — under
# `if ! curl`, $? would report the negation's status, not curl's.)
curl_rc=0
curl -fsSL --max-time 60 --retry 2 "$MANIFEST_URL" \
  -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/pin-manifest.json" || curl_rc=$?
if [ "$curl_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::pin-freshness: FAIL — could not fetch ${MANIFEST_URL} (curl rc=${curl_rc}). Before the S2 cutover this is expected (the landing does not serve the manifest yet); after it, this is the broken-landing / missed-dispatch signal R22 exists for."
  exit 1
fi

served_sha="$(node -e '
  const fs = require("node:fs");
  let m;
  try { m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8")); }
  catch (e) {
    console.error("pin-freshness: FAIL — manifest is not valid JSON: " + e.message);
    process.exit(2);
  }
  const sha = m["verified-at"] ?? (m.framework && m.framework["verified-at"]);
  if (typeof sha !== "string" || !/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(sha)) {
    console.error("pin-freshness: FAIL — " + process.env.MANIFEST_URL + " carries no usable verified-at SHA (found: " + JSON.stringify(sha) + "); expected the D8b/FD11 field: verified-at = 40-hex framework sha");
    process.exit(2);
  }
  process.stdout.write(sha);
' "$RUNNER_TEMP/pin-manifest.json")"
echo "pin-freshness: served manifest verifies at ${served_sha}"

if [ "$served_sha" = "$main_sha" ]; then
  echo "pin-freshness: PASS — the published site verifies at origin/main (${main_sha})"
  exit 0
fi

if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$served_sha" "$main_sha"; then
  echo "::error::pin-freshness: FAIL — served verified-at ${served_sha} is NOT an ancestor of origin/main ${main_sha}. The published site was built from something main does not contain (pre-cutover pin, or a misresolved framework.pin)."
  exit 1
fi

served_epoch="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$served_sha")"
now_epoch="$(date +%s)"
age_hours=$(( (now_epoch - served_epoch) / 3600 ))
if [ "$age_hours" -ge "$STALE_BUDGET_HOURS" ]; then
  echo "::error::pin-freshness: FAIL — the published site verifies at ${served_sha:0:12}, ${age_hours} h behind origin/main ${main_sha:0:12} (budget ${STALE_BUDGET_HOURS} h, R22). One of: a promote that never dispatched, a dispatch that never fired, or a red landing build."
  exit 1
fi

echo "::warning::pin-freshness: NOTICE — the published site verifies at ${served_sha:0:12}, ${age_hours} h behind origin/main (within the ${STALE_BUDGET_HOURS} h budget); the promote→dispatch→deploy chain is in flight."
exit 0

name: Check REQUIRED_CONTEXTS against staging branch protection (best-effort)

invocation.name: Check REQUIRED_CONTEXTS against staging branch protection (best-effort)
invocation.run:
# Tri-state semantics (read the KNOWN LIMITATION above first — with GITHUB_TOKEN
# the third arm is the NORMAL outcome, not the exception):
#   - state READABLE and includes every REQUIRED_CONTEXTS entry → pass
#   - state READABLE but an entry is missing → fail (R11 violated)
#   - state UNREADABLE (no admin scope) or genuinely unconfigured → warn, pass;
#     these two are indistinguishable from here, so the warning says UNDETERMINED
# Rationale for passing on the third arm: a repo that has not configured branch
# protection must not be blocked. The cost is that R11 enforcement does NOT
# "kick in automatically" once protection is configured — the API stays
# unreadable to this token, so the check keeps warn-passing (measured, PR #1102).
# Making it real requires an admin-scoped PAT secret (operator decision).

protection_json="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/branches/staging/protection" 2>/dev/null || echo 'null')"
rulesets_json="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/rulesets" 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"

has_protection=$(echo "$protection_json" | jq 'if . == null or (type=="object" and has("message")) then false else true end')
has_rulesets=$(echo "$rulesets_json" | jq 'if type=="array" then [.[] | select(.enforcement == "active")] | length > 0 else false end')

# REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: every check whose fail-closed property rests on being a
# REQUIRED status check on staging. Listing a context here does NOT make that
# precondition a mechanism — with GITHUB_TOKEN this check cannot read the protection
# state (KNOWN LIMITATION above), so registration remains operator-enforced
# (`#hope-as-gate`) until an admin-scoped credential exists. The list is kept because
# it is correct wherever the state IS readable.
#
# DERIVED, NOT AUTHORED. This list is NOT the source of truth and must not be edited
# by hand alone: each entry is declared at its own job by a `# required-context: yes`
# marker, and packages/core/principles/37-required-context-completeness.test.ts asserts
# this list equals the declared set exactly (and that scripts/run-local-ci-sweep.sh's
# `# REQUIRED_CONTEXTS:` block does too). Until principle 37 shipped, this comment
# claimed to be "the single place recording which contexts must be registered" — it was
# neither single (the sweep held a second list) nor current (`stale-revert-in-pr-diff`
# had been registered on staging and was missing here). Change a job's marker or its
# `name:`, run the principles suite, and update all three together.
#
# RENAME HAZARD: an entry is a job's `name:` verbatim. Renaming a declared-required job
# keeps this gate green (marker and list move together) while branch protection still
# points at the OLD string — a context that never reports, deadlocking every PR. Any
# such rename must be paired with a re-registration in Settings → Branches.
required_contexts='[
  "Template render probes — P1/P4/P6 (deterministic)",
  "capability PR carries Prior-art line in PR body (squash-survival)",
  "ci-success",
  "fidelity-verdict-in-pr-body",
  "stale-revert-in-pr-diff",
  "§1.7 forward+backward sections present in PR description"
]'

if [ "$has_protection" = "true" ]; then
  missing="$(echo "$protection_json" | jq -r --argjson want "$required_contexts" \
    '($want - (.required_status_checks.contexts // [])) | join(", ")')"
  if [ -z "$missing" ]; then
    echo "✅ required checks present on staging (classic branch protection): $required_contexts"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::Branch protection exists on staging but these required status checks are MISSING: ${missing} (R11 violated)."
  echo "::error::Settings → Branches → staging → Require status checks → add: ${missing}"
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$has_rulesets" = "true" ]; then
  echo "✅ rulesets active — manually verify ${required_contexts} in https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/settings/rules"
  exit 0
fi

# Reaching here means the API returned nothing readable. With GITHUB_TOKEN that
# is the NORMAL case even when protection exists (admin read is unavailable to
# any workflow permission scope — measured PR #1102), so this must NOT claim
# protection is absent: it cannot tell "absent" from "unreadable".
echo "::warning::UNDETERMINED: cannot read staging branch protection with this token (admin read is not grantable to GITHUB_TOKEN), so R11 compliance is UNVERIFIED — this job's success does NOT mean the required contexts are registered."
echo "::warning::Verify manually: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/staging/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts' → must contain ${required_contexts}"
exit 0

invocation.name: Install dependencies (own package manager — literal detect_pm ladder below)
invocation.run:
set -e
# ownPM selection — the detect_pm ladder verbatim (lib.sh:2460-2474, sha 3ce99cf9…).
# Workflow cwd is GITHUB_WORKSPACE = repo root = the $PROJECT_ROOT detect_pm reads.
if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ] || [ -f pnpm-workspace.yaml ]; then PM=pnpm
elif [ -f yarn.lock ] || [ -f .yarnrc.yml ]; then PM=yarn
else PM=npm
fi
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f package.json ]; then
  field=$(AIF_PJ=package.json node -e 'try{const m=(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.env.AIF_PJ,"utf8")).packageManager||"").split("@")[0];if(["npm","pnpm","yarn"].includes(m))process.stdout.write(m)}catch{}' 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ -n "$field" ] && PM="$field"
fi
echo "getff: own package manager selected: $PM"
# Install with the SELECTED own PM only — its own lock/no-lock policy. NO cross-PM
# fallback anywhere: an unavailable tool fails this step loudly (set -e), it never
# silently installs via another manager.
case "$PM" in
  pnpm)
    corepack enable
    if [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; else pnpm install; fi ;;
  yarn)
    corepack enable
    # Modern Yarn defaults immutable=TRUE under CI (yarnpkg.com/cli/install) and then
    # aborts when resolution must create a lockfile. No-lock installs therefore carry
    # an EXPLICIT non-immutable flag (the negation of that same documented setting);
    # lock-present installs stay immutable via the --frozen-lockfile alias.
    if [ -f yarn.lock ]; then yarn install --frozen-lockfile; else yarn install --no-immutable; fi ;;
  npm)
    if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then npm ci --prefer-offline; else npm install --no-audit --no-fund; fi ;;
esac

invocation.name: Stryker on diff only
invocation.run:
CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF...HEAD" \
  | grep -E '^src/.+\.(ts|tsx)$' \
  | grep -v -E '\.(test|spec|stories)\.(ts|tsx)$' \
  | tr '\n' ',' || true)
if [ -n "$CHANGED" ]; then
  npx stryker run --mutate "$CHANGED" --incremental
else
  echo "No src/ changes — skipping Stryker"
fi

invocation.name: Assert ci-success is a required status check on the default branch
invocation.run:
# Tri-state semantics:
#   - protection or rulesets configured AND include ci-success → pass
#   - protection or rulesets configured but ci-success missing → fail (R11 violated)
#   - no protection AND no rulesets → warn, pass (not yet adopted, OR permanently
#     unavailable on a GitHub Free private repo — protection/rulesets need GitHub Pro)
# Rationale: don't block PRs in repos that haven't yet configured branch
# protection. Once configured, R11 enforcement kicks in automatically.

protection_json="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/branches/${DEFAULT_BRANCH}/protection" 2>/dev/null || echo 'null')"
rulesets_json="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/rulesets" 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"

has_protection=$(echo "$protection_json" | jq 'if . == null or (type=="object" and has("message")) then false else true end')
has_rulesets=$(echo "$rulesets_json" | jq 'if type=="array" then [.[] | select(.enforcement == "active")] | length > 0 else false end')

if [ "$has_protection" = "true" ]; then
  if echo "$protection_json" | jq -e '.required_status_checks.contexts | contains(["ci-success"])' > /dev/null; then
    echo "✅ ci-success is required on ${DEFAULT_BRANCH} (classic branch protection)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::Branch protection exists on ${DEFAULT_BRANCH} but ci-success is NOT in required status checks (R11 violated)."
  echo "::error::Settings → Branches → ${DEFAULT_BRANCH} → Require status checks → ci-success"
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$has_rulesets" = "true" ]; then
  echo "✅ rulesets active — manually verify ci-success in https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/settings/rules"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::warning::No branch protection or active rulesets on ${DEFAULT_BRANCH}. R11 branch-protection is not active — either not yet adopted, or unavailable on a GitHub Free private repo (classic protection and rulesets require GitHub Pro, or a public repo)."
echo "::warning::To enable (needs a public repo, or GitHub Pro/Team for private): Settings → Branches → ${DEFAULT_BRANCH} → Require status checks → ci-success"
exit 0
